\textbf{\LARGE 9.3 Telescoping Sums Worksheet --- Solutions}

\vspace{10pt}

\typehead{Telescoping Sums}{\textbf{Method:} (1) Use partial fractions (or log rules) to write each term as a difference $u_k = b_k - b_{k+m}$. (2) Write out $s_n$ and cancel the inner terms to get a closed form. (3) The sum of the series is $\lim_{n\to+\infty} s_n$; if the limit does not exist, the series diverges.}

\problem{1.}{\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{k^{2}+3k+2} = \frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{12} + \frac{1}{20} + \cdots + \frac{1}{k^{2}+3k+2} + \cdots}

\step{Partial fractions.} $k^2 + 3k + 2 = (k+1)(k+2)$, and
$$
\frac{1}{(k+1)(k+2)} = \frac{1}{k+1} - \frac{1}{k+2}.
$$

\step{Partial sum.}
$$
s_n = \left(\frac12 - \frac13\right) + \left(\frac13 - \frac14\right) + \cdots + \left(\frac{1}{n+1} - \frac{1}{n+2}\right) = \frac12 - \frac{1}{n+2}.
$$

\step{Limit.} $\displaystyle \lim_{n\to+\infty} s_n = \lim_{n\to+\infty}\left(\frac12 - \frac{1}{n+2}\right) = \frac12.$
\answer{converges, sum $= \dfrac12$}

\problem{2.}{\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{(2k-1)(2k+1)} = \frac{1}{1\cdot 3} + \frac{1}{3\cdot 5} + \frac{1}{5\cdot 7} + \cdots}

\step{Partial fractions.}
$$
\frac{1}{(2k-1)(2k+1)} = \frac12\left(\frac{1}{2k-1} - \frac{1}{2k+1}\right).
$$

\step{Partial sum.}
$$
s_n = \frac12\left[\left(1 - \frac13\right) + \left(\frac13 - \frac15\right) + \cdots + \left(\frac{1}{2n-1} - \frac{1}{2n+1}\right)\right] = \frac12\left(1 - \frac{1}{2n+1}\right).
$$

\step{Limit.} $\displaystyle \lim_{n\to+\infty} s_n = \frac12(1 - 0) = \frac12.$
\answer{converges, sum $= \dfrac12$}

\problem{3.}{\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \ln\!\left(\frac{k}{k+1}\right) = \ln\frac12 + \ln\frac23 + \ln\frac34 + \cdots}

\step{Log rule.} $\ln\!\left(\dfrac{k}{k+1}\right) = \ln k - \ln(k+1)$.

\step{Partial sum.}
$$
s_n = (\ln 1 - \ln 2) + (\ln 2 - \ln 3) + \cdots + (\ln n - \ln(n+1)) = \ln 1 - \ln(n+1) = -\ln(n+1).
$$

\step{Limit.} $\displaystyle \lim_{n\to+\infty} s_n = \lim_{n\to+\infty}\big(-\ln(n+1)\big) = -\infty$, so the limit does not exist.
\answer{diverges}

\problem{4.}{\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{2}{k(k+2)} = \frac{2}{1\cdot 3} + \frac{2}{2\cdot 4} + \frac{2}{3\cdot 5} + \cdots}

\step{Partial fractions.}
$$
\frac{2}{k(k+2)} = \frac1k - \frac{1}{k+2}.
$$

\step{Partial sum.} Now terms cancel \emph{two apart}, so two positive terms survive at the start and two negative terms at the end:
$$
\begin{aligned}
s_n &= \left(1 - \frac13\right) + \left(\frac12 - \frac14\right) + \left(\frac13 - \frac15\right) + \cdots + \left(\frac{1}{n-1} - \frac{1}{n+1}\right) + \left(\frac1n - \frac{1}{n+2}\right) \\
&= 1 + \frac12 - \frac{1}{n+1} - \frac{1}{n+2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

\step{Limit.} $\displaystyle \lim_{n\to+\infty} s_n = 1 + \frac12 - 0 - 0 = \frac32.$
\answer{converges, sum $= \dfrac32$}

\problem{5.}{\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{4}{k^{2}+4k+3} = \frac{4}{2\cdot 4} + \frac{4}{3\cdot 5} + \frac{4}{4\cdot 6} + \cdots}

\step{Partial fractions.} $k^2 + 4k + 3 = (k+1)(k+3)$, and
$$
\frac{4}{(k+1)(k+3)} = \frac{2}{k+1} - \frac{2}{k+3}.
$$

\step{Partial sum.} Terms cancel two apart:
$$
\begin{aligned}
s_n &= 2\left[\left(\frac12 - \frac14\right) + \left(\frac13 - \frac15\right) + \left(\frac14 - \frac16\right) + \cdots + \left(\frac{1}{n+1} - \frac{1}{n+3}\right)\right] \\
&= 2\left(\frac12 + \frac13 - \frac{1}{n+2} - \frac{1}{n+3}\right).
\end{aligned}
$$

\step{Limit.} $\displaystyle \lim_{n\to+\infty} s_n = 2\left(\frac12 + \frac13\right) = 2\cdot\frac56 = \frac53.$
\answer{converges, sum $= \dfrac53$}

\problem{6.}{\frac{1}{4\cdot 5} + \frac{1}{5\cdot 6} + \frac{1}{6\cdot 7} + \cdots + \frac{1}{(k+3)(k+4)} + \cdots}

\step{Sigma form.} This is $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{(k+3)(k+4)}$ (check: $k=1$ gives $\frac{1}{4\cdot 5}$).

\step{Partial fractions.}
$$
\frac{1}{(k+3)(k+4)} = \frac{1}{k+3} - \frac{1}{k+4}.
$$

\step{Partial sum.}
$$
s_n = \left(\frac14 - \frac15\right) + \left(\frac15 - \frac16\right) + \cdots + \left(\frac{1}{n+3} - \frac{1}{n+4}\right) = \frac14 - \frac{1}{n+4}.
$$

\step{Limit.} $\displaystyle \lim_{n\to+\infty} s_n = \frac14.$
\answer{converges, sum $= \dfrac14$}

\problem{7.}{\frac{1}{1\cdot 4} + \frac{1}{4\cdot 7} + \frac{1}{7\cdot 10} + \cdots + \frac{1}{(3k-2)(3k+1)} + \cdots}

\step{Sigma form.} This is $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{(3k-2)(3k+1)}$ (check: $k=1$ gives $\frac{1}{1\cdot 4}$).

\step{Partial fractions.} The factors differ by $3$, so
$$
\frac{1}{(3k-2)(3k+1)} = \frac13\left(\frac{1}{3k-2} - \frac{1}{3k+1}\right).
$$

\step{Partial sum.}
$$
s_n = \frac13\left[\left(1 - \frac14\right) + \left(\frac14 - \frac17\right) + \cdots + \left(\frac{1}{3n-2} - \frac{1}{3n+1}\right)\right] = \frac13\left(1 - \frac{1}{3n+1}\right).
$$

\step{Limit.} $\displaystyle \lim_{n\to+\infty} s_n = \frac13(1 - 0) = \frac13.$
\answer{converges, sum $= \dfrac13$}
